name: context_relevance
title: Context compaction: keep, summarize, or drop
description: For a coding/agent session near its context limit, decide what to do with each chunk of prior context given the current goal: keep it, how important it is, its role, and whether its exact text must be preserved.
writes: one chunk of an AI coding agent's session context paired with the task it is currently working on. The chunk is one of: a tool/command output, a file or diff excerpt, a user message, an assistant message, an error/stack trace, or a plan. Make the chunk concrete (real-looking code, paths, commands, or prose) and vary how related it is to the goal.

fields.current_goal: what the agent is working on right now, 1-2 sentences
fields.chunk: the one piece of prior context being judged: its kind and its content (5-20 short lines)

ask: Should this chunk be kept in context for the current goal?
Is this chunk still worth its tokens?

labels.yes: needed or useful for what the agent is doing now
labels.no: can be dropped without hurting the current goal

ask: How important is it to retain this chunk?

labels.high: central to the current goal; losing it would break the work

ask: What is this chunk's role relative to the current goal?

labels.active_work: directly part of what is being done now
labels.reference: background or an earlier result that may be needed again
labels.stale: finished or obsolete; the work it belonged to is done
labels.superseded: replaced by newer information in the session

ask: How should this chunk be compacted?

labels.verbatim: exact text matters: code, commands, IDs, paths, error messages, numbers
labels.summarize: the gist is enough; details can be dropped
